test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is correct about engine valves?

options.text: The camshaft and its associated parts control the flame of sparks during ignition of the enigne.
Poppet or mushroom valves are commonly found in two stroke engines for their remarkable features.
The valve’s head is perfectly positioned at a 30-45 degree angle that ideally fits with the valve seat, creating a firm seal.
Valves with their conical shapes control the flow of the entry of gasses into an engine.

solution:
The correct answer is __The valve’s head is perfectly positioned at a 30-45 degree angle that ideally fits with the valve seat, creating a firm seal.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Engine valves__ are crucial components in the functioning of an engine.
 
• The valve’s head is designed at a 30-45 degree angle, ensuring a precise and firm seal with the valve seat.
 
• This seal is essential to regulate the flow of gases during the intake and exhaust cycles.
 
• Poppet or mushroom valves are commonly found in four-stroke engines, not two-stroke engines.
 
• Camshaft controls the opening and closing of valves, not the flame of sparks during ignition.
 
• Valves with conical shapes are used to control the gas flow in an engine efficiently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Camshaft:**

 
 
• The camshaft is a rotating shaft that actuates the opening and closing of engine valves.
 
• It is synchronized with the crankshaft to ensure proper timing.
 
 
 
• **Valve Types:**
 
 
• Poppet valves are the most common type, featuring a mushroom-like shape.
 
• Other types include sleeve valves and rotary valves used in specific engine designs.
 
 
 
• **Two-Stroke Engines:**
 
 
• Unlike four-stroke engines, two-stroke engines rely on ports instead of valves for gas exchange.
 
• This design simplifies the engine structure but limits control over gas flow.
